name: Spain

findings.controller: Ericsson (5G core control plane) and Nokia (5G core user plane)
findings.summary: Telefónica España completed awarding its 5G core: Ericsson took the control plane in 2021 and Nokia the user plane in January 2025 (about €15m over six years), with region-by-region migration.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson (Sweden) and Nokia (Finland) are third-pole vendors. The €15m Nokia figure is a press estimate, not converted to USD. Migration completion was not confirmed in this pass.

findings.reversal_of: Huawei 5G core network at Telefónica España (2019 award)
findings.summary: Telefónica removed Huawei, awarded its 5G core in 2019, from the core network after international pressure, awarding the replacement to Ericsson and Nokia; Orange and Vodafone had already dropped Huawei from their 5G cores.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded as reversal of the 2019 Huawei 5G core award (tier 3). Sources attribute it to international/US pressure and an indirect Spanish ban via exclusion of high-risk suppliers from 5G subsidies, so geopolitical. Euronews reports Huawei sued in the Audiencia Nacional over exclusion from rural 5G aid. Audit 2026-10-28: Xataka (2025-01-24): the Nokia migration was rolling out region by region and expected to take over a year, so the swap was awarded, not complete, in Jan 2025.

findings.summary: Vodafone in Spain still ran about 70% of its radio network on Huawei equipment in early 2025, though it had already dropped Huawei from its 5G core.
findings.analyst_inference: Operational legacy RAN (2G-4G), so tier 5. Vodafone España has since changed ownership (Zegona); any later swap plan was not checked. Audit 2026-10-28: Neither cited source names Nokia as 5G core vendor, the 2023 date or Nokia/Ericsson 5G radio; those details removed.

findings.reversal_of: Huawei radio access network at MasOrange (phase-out planned by 2028)
findings.summary: MasOrange plans to cut Huawei's share of its radio network from 54% to 39% by 2027 and remove it entirely from 2028; its 5G core is already Huawei-free.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded as a planned reversal of operational Huawei legacy RAN. Neither source gives MasOrange's own reason; coded commercial for lack of a stated geopolitical rationale, though the general context sources describe is a de facto Huawei exclusion. Audit 2026-10-28: The sources confirm only a Huawei-free 5G core, not European 5G radio; Xataka calls the operator Orange. Tier-5 reversal for a plan not yet executed is a coding question for Brian.

findings.reversal_of: RedIRIS capacity upgrade contract specifying Huawei routers (Telefónica as bidder)
findings.summary: The government cancelled a roughly €10m tender, proposed for award to Telefónica, to upgrade the RedIRIS research backbone with Huawei routing equipment, citing digital strategy and strategic autonomy; a new tender is planned.
findings.analyst_inference: The contracting board had proposed Telefónica's bid; formalisation status at cancellation is unclear, so tier 3 is an upper bound. The stated rationale (European/Spanish sovereignty) and reported US/EU warnings support geopolitical. Existing RedIRIS IP gear remains Huawei, near end of life. Audit 2026-10-28: El Independiente: tender 24 Jul 2025, board proposed Telefónica 25 Aug 2025, formal award not stated, Huawei not ruled out of the new tender; a dplnews headline (not read) suggests a later re-tender.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of the Interior (SITEL lawful interception)
findings.summary: The Interior Ministry awarded Huawei €12.3m in contracts to store judicially authorised wiretaps for police and intelligence use on Huawei OceanStor storage, under a 2021-2025 framework and CCN security guidelines.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor is the controller under the v0.2 rule. USD figure (~$14.3m) is The Record's conversion and left null here. No cancellation found. A Dec 2025 Vozpópuli report of a small (€17,916) Policía Nacional purchase of Huawei-compatible storage expansion suggests Huawei storage was still in use, but it was not tied to SITEL specifically.

findings.local_actor: Guardia Civil (Benasal barracks), Ministry of the Interior
findings.summary: An Interior Ministry contract for the Guardia Civil barracks in Benasal specified Hikvision mini-dome cameras and Dahua video recorders; The Objective reports dozens of similar Interior and Defence surveillance contracts.
findings.analyst_inference: Single site, so municipal scale; the wider 'dozens of contracts' claim was not individually verified. Supplier was a Spanish integrator (Alarmas Llorca); value not given.

findings.summary: AWS pledged €15.7bn through 2033 to expand its data-centre footprint in Spain, centred on its existing Aragón region sites.
findings.analyst_inference: Investment pledge, so tier 1; the existing AWS region is covered by the global cloud layer. An Aug 2025 headline (not opened) says the expansion's path was cleared; construction status not confirmed. EUR value not converted.

findings.summary: Aragón's government gave initial approval to Microsoft's plan for three data-centre campuses (La Muela, Villamayor de Gállego, Zaragoza; ~284 ha) with building costs above €5.3bn; construction awaits final approval.
findings.analyst_inference: Initial planning approval coded as tier 2 (pre-construction). The $6.17bn conversion is DCD's and is a building-cost estimate; left null. Final approval and construction start after Nov 2025 not checked. Audit 2026-10-28: No final approval or construction start found after the Nov 2025 initial approval.

findings.summary: Aragón declared Blackstone's €7.5bn 'Proyecto Rodes' data-centre campus at Calatorao (224 ha) a project of regional general interest, opening permitting; not yet under construction.
findings.analyst_inference: Blackstone is a US fund, so us as owner-operator; tenant unknown. Planning declaration coded tier 2. A later snippet (ecosistemastartup, S5, not cited) mentions a larger €11.8bn figure; not verified. Audit 2026-10-28: El Español (2026-07-28) reports environmental approval in July 2026; total €11.8bn, €7.5bn first phase; construction not started.

findings.financier: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking and Spain-Portugal-Turkey consortium
findings.summary: MareNostrum 5, an Atos-built EuroHPC supercomputer hosted at BSC, uses Nvidia Hopper GPUs with Intel Sapphire Rapids CPUs in its main accelerated partition; it was in production use training Spain's ALIA models from 2024.
findings.analyst_inference: Hardware is from HPCwire's 2022 procurement report (€151.4m, split between EuroHPC JU and a Spain/Portugal/Turkey consortium); operational use is from Xataka's ALIA report. The sources cover different facts, so not counted as corroboration. H100 count not found. Audit 2026-10-28: HPCwire says Hopper (not H100 explicitly) and lists Lenovo ThinkSystem alongside Atos; ALIA training use not re-verified.

findings.summary: Prime Minister Sánchez launched ALIA, a publicly funded family of Spanish and co-official-language models (2B-40B) trained from scratch on MareNostrum 5 and released under Apache 2.0; first uses include a Tax Agency chatbot pilot.
findings.analyst_inference: Weights held by a Spanish public centre, so domestic. Llama-style architecture but trained from zero-initialised weights, so base_model null. Tier 2 because government uses were announced as initial pilots; deployment at scale not confirmed. No S1/S2 opened (BSC page blocked).

power.null_reason: no AI/data-centre-dedicated power plant surfaced in facilities searches; budget spent on higher-priority layers

research_gaps: Is the Interior Ministry's Huawei wiretap-storage (SITEL) arrangement still in force after the 2021-2025 framework ended, and was it re-tendered without Huawei following US/EU warnings?
Was the RedIRIS router tender re-issued, and which vendor won?
Has Spain published the high-risk 5G supplier list provided for in its 5G cybersecurity law, and what happened to Huawei's Audiencia Nacional lawsuit over rural 5G aid exclusion?
Vodafone España (Zegona) plans for its ~70% Huawei legacy RAN; MasOrange progress against its 2027/2028 Huawei phase-out targets.
Microsoft Aragón campuses: final PIGA approval and construction start; Blackstone Calatorao and ACS Zaragoza campuses: status, controller and tenants.
MareNostrum 5 AI upgrades or Spanish AI Factory (EuroHPC) accelerator purchases since 2025, and any other large Nvidia/AMD deployments (e.g. Telefónica, Meta Talavera).
Any national-government agreement with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral or others; actual scale of ALIA adoption in public administration.
Extent of Hikvision/Dahua cameras across Interior and Defence sites (The Objective's 'dozens of contracts') and any municipal safe-city deployments.
